newsitem.title: USA: Oregon 1995-97 budget revs estimated at $7.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: Oregon 1995-97 budget revs estimated at $7.5 bln.

text.p: Oregon is forecast to end the 1995-1997 biennium with general fund revenues of nearly $7.5 billion, an increase of $61.7 million from the December estimate, budget officials said Friday.

The state Office of Economic Analysis, in its March revenue report, said the $7.461 billion 1995-1997 general fund revenue forecast was nearly $500 million greater than the 1995 Close of Legislative Session (COS) forecast.

The Office of Economic Analysis said the revised budget forecast reflects a $38.3 million projected increase in corporate income taxes, a $13 million increase in general fund interest earnings and an $8.5 million increase in personal income tax revenues.
State lottery revenues are forecast at $715.3 million, an increase of $8.5 million from the December estimate. The March forecast is $53.6 million below the 1995 COS estimate.
